name: Perspective grid
summary: Lines that run to one vanishing point on a horizon, so that a flat surface reads as a floor in deep space.
how: Put the horizon at 50% to 65% of the height and draw 12 to 24 lines to one vanishing point.
Space the cross lines so that each gap is about 0.8 of the gap in front of it.

origin.note: Filippo Brunelleschi demonstrates linear perspective; Alberti writes the method down in De pictura (1435).

adoptions.via: Stanley Kubrick sets corridors and rooms on one central vanishing point in 2001: A Space Odyssey; Wes Anderson later builds whole films on the flat, centred frame.
Cassette Futurism screens and sleeves draw wireframe floors to a horizon.
Tron draws vector grids that run to a horizon.
Vaporwave draws neon grid floors under a sunset.
